---
title: "A page of your own"
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    collapse: true
    comment: "#>"
---

ogis draws maps; it does not edit data. A page that lets a reader do something more (mark features, write a
verdict of your own, move a label) is yours, built on the map with two calls: `og_script()` puts your script into the
page, and `og_serve(routes = )` gives it routes of its own on the server. The script is given one object, `og`, the
whole of what it may use of the page (the help of `og_script()` lists it):

| `og.` | gives |
|---|---|
| `map` | MapLibre's map |
| `layer(id)` | a layer's MapLibre style ids, source and key |
| `on("click", id, fn)` | a click on a layer's features, its row as `row()` |
| `state(id, key, value)` | a feature's state in MapLibre, which its styles read |
| `setData(id, geojson)` | new data for a layer sent whole |
| `filter(id, key, expr)` | a filter of your own, kept with the page's choices |
| `panel(title)` | a box in the sidebar, yours to fill |
| `fetch(name, init)` | your route `name` on the server, a path and a query after it if any (`"marks/12?full=1"`); `og.served` is false in a bundle |
| `save(name, text)` | a file handed to the reader |

## A list of marked positions

A click on a position adds its vessel and time to a list in a panel, and rings it on the map; a button saves the list.
On a server, the list goes to the route `marks`; in a bundle, which has no server (as on this page), the reader is
handed a file.

The ring is MapLibre's own feature state. Each feature of a layer function is known by its row's number, the
`feature.id` of a click; `og.state()` sets a state on it, and the layer's style reads it as `feature-state`, given in
MapLibre's own terms. Nothing is sent again, and the state stays through a change of base map.

```{r}
library(ogis)

js <- r"(
  const body = og.panel("Marked");
  const list = document.createElement("ol"), save = document.createElement("button");
  save.textContent = "Save the list";
  body.append(list, save);
  const marks = [];
  og.on("click", "positions", async ({ feature, row }) => {
    og.state("positions", feature.id, { marked: true });
    const r = await row();
    if (!r) return;                       // clicked again meanwhile
    const v = Object.fromEntries(r.map(c => [c.name, c.value]));
    marks.push(v);
    list.append(Object.assign(document.createElement("li"),
                              { textContent: `${v.vid} at ${v.time}` }));
  });
  save.onclick = () => og.served
    ? og.fetch("marks", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(marks) })
    : og.save("marks.csv", "vid,time\n" + marks.map(m => `${m.vid},${m.time}`).join("\n"));
)"

marked <- function(yes, no) {
  list("case", list("boolean", list("feature-state", "marked"), FALSE), yes, no)
}
m <- og_example("trawlsurvey") |>
  og_point(colour = behaviour, popup = c(vid, time), id = "positions",
           name = "Positions",
           "circle-stroke-width" = marked(3, 0),
           "circle-stroke-color" = marked("#000000", "#ffffff")) |>
  og_script(js)
m
```

Click a few positions, then *Save the list*.

## Its route on the server

Served from R, the route writes what the page sends to a file, a row a mark, never rewriting it. A route's function is
given the request (`method`, `path`, `query`, `body`, a JSON body read into R) and returns what goes back: a list as
JSON. Keep it fast: the server answers one request at a time.

```{r}
#| eval: false
file <- "marks.csv"
og_serve(m, routes = list(marks = function(req) {
  write.table(req$body, file, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE,
              col.names = !file.exists(file), append = file.exists(file))
  list(saved = nrow(req$body))
}))
```

In a script run by `Rscript`, give `og_serve(..., wait = TRUE)`: it keeps serving until stopped (Ctrl-C). In
RStudio it answers while the console is idle. The page's writes are answered only for a page opened from this computer.
